claims.original_claim: The cause was that the guard read 'if rf <= 0.0', which NaN passes because NaN compares False against every ordering and equality operator (it returns True against !=), and which infinity passes because infinity is legitimately positive; and the module already contained a _is_finite helper that _as_resistance never called.
claims.auditor_observed: Pre-change resistance guard only tests rf<=0 and does not call the existing finite helper.

claims.original_claim: WITHDRAWN BY THE AUTHOR BEFORE HANDOVER. I called i_pred(8.0, inf) -> 0.0 the dangerous one because a zero flow reads downstream as a starved path, and the changelog went further and called it an ASOM classification produced from garbage. BOTH ARE WRONG. There is no code path from a flow number to an ASOM label: asom() takes two enums, asom(0.0, INTENDED) returns None, and Region is always a caller judgement. Measured through delta_current, the module's only numeric consumer of a flow value: 0.0 -> OVERSHOOT (visible), nan -> WITHIN_TOLERANCE (the SAME sign reading as a perfectly correct prediction), inf -> UNDERSHOOT. NaN is the dangerous value, not 0.0. I picked the wrong value and stated the wrong mechanism.
claims.auditor_observed: asom(0.0,INTENDED)->None; delta prediction2,0,nan,inf gives WITHIN_TOLERANCE,OVERSHOOT,WITHIN_TOLERANCE,UNDERSHOOT. Known NaN defect remains live.
